faq_heading: New construction in Port Coquitlam: your questions answered

faq.q: What counts as new construction on this page?
faq.a: Active MLS® listings in Port Coquitlam where the board's age field is 0 or less: homes finished this year and homes listed before completion, in houses, townhomes and condos.

faq.q: Where are the newest homes in Port Coquitlam?
faq.a: Over the past year the newest sold homes were duplexes in Glenwood PQ: median build year 2026, 9 sales, median price $1,028,571.

faq.q: How fast do newer homes sell in Port Coquitlam?
faq.a: The quickest group among the newer ones was duplexes in Glenwood PQ: 14 days to sell at a median, closing at 95.5% of the list price.

blocks.text: What newer homes in Port Coquitlam have sold for
In November 2025 to October 2026, duplexes in Glenwood PQ had the newest stock of any Port Coquitlam sub-area with enough sales to measure: median build year 2026, 9 sales, median price $1,028,571.
2 of 20 sub-area and home-type groups with 5 or more sales had a median build year of 2020 or later. The newest were Glenwood PQ duplexes (built 2026) and Central Pt Coquitlam townhomes (built 2024).

items.t: Glenwood PQ duplexes: 9 sold at a median of $1,028,571 (middle half between $951,428 and $1,088,888), taking 14 days at 95.5% of the list price, with a median build year of 2026. The typical home had 3 bedrooms, it sold for about $634 per square foot and 0% of the sales closed over the list price.

In Central Pt Coquitlam, the 24 townhomes that sold had a median build year of 2024 and a median price of $999,950; the middle half closed between $757,500 and $1,054,900, after 18 days on the market at 100.0% of list. The typical home had 3 bedrooms, it sold for about $611 per square foot, strata fees were a median $389 a month and 8% of the sales closed over the list price.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam overall: what sold over the past year

items.t: Across Port Coquitlam, 168 houses sold at a median of $1,295,000, with the middle half between $1,182,500 and $1,420,000. They took 21 days and closed at 96.7% of the list price, and the median build year was 1978. The typical house sat on a lot of about 6,048 square feet. The median moved from $1,335,000 (November to January) to $1,220,000 (August to October).

Port Coquitlam townhomes over the past year: 155 sales, a median of $878,000, and a middle half from $800,000 to $1,000,000. The median home was built in 2002, took 19 days to sell and closed at 97.9% of list. Strata fees were a median $407 a month. The median moved from $905,000 (November to January) to $815,000 (August to October).

Across Port Coquitlam, 202 condos sold at a median of $557,500, with the middle half between $465,625 and $628,375. They took 28 days and closed at 97.6% of the list price, and the median build year was 2008. Strata fees were a median $431 a month. The median moved from $607,500 (November to January) to $545,000 (August to October).

Port Coquitlam duplexes over the past year: 16 sales, a median of $1,044,000, and a middle half from $951,428 to $1,107,250. The median home was built in 2026, took 24 days to sell and closed at 97.7% of list.

blocks.text: Planning and zoning notes for Port Coquitlam

items.t: Port Coquitlam's Official Community Plan (Bylaw 3838) plans the Dominion Riverfront for townhouses and low-rise apartments. It names Lincoln Park and Mary Hill as neighbourhoods developed from the 1950s, and Riverwood and Citadel Heights as 1980s and 1990s neighbourhoods.
